clue.text: State embargo inter alia?

indicators.note: Latin for 'between' or 'among', so the ban word is placed among the letters of alia

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: A legal-sounding note that an embargo was one measure among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' reads as the Latin phrase 'among other things'; split it, and 'inter' (Latin 'among') is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a sovereign nation in the Balkans, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: Seaman loves concocting excuse

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: concocting means cooking up, so the letters of loves are mixed

explanation.surface: A sailor in love invents an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free from blame, which is to excuse or pardon.

clue.text: Lady-killer — indecent animal — died

parts.note: blue means risqué or indecent, as in blue jokes
a bear is an animal
D is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A womaniser described as a crude beast now dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebeard is the folk-tale husband who murdered his wives, a literal killer of ladies.

clue.text: Deepest point in Mahanadi river

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The river's lowest stretch, in an Indian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mahanadi is a real river in eastern India.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Answer long rambling question in native language

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters of long are rearranged

explanation.surface: Giving a long, wandering answer to a question in a native tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Algonquin is the language of an indigenous people of Canada, a Native American tongue.

clue.text: Attack persistently dismal crowd in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the dismal crowd is read from the end

parts.note: dismal means drab
a crowd is a mob

explanation.surface: A gloomy mob falling back from the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to assail with a sustained barrage, of shells or of questions.

clue.text: It has branches in Strand we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for strand is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a strand is a shore, a beach

explanation.surface: Something with branches in London's Strand, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' is capitalised to suggest the London street; here it is a shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A beech is a tree, and trees have branches.

clue.text: Grow up around home with single baby

indicators.note: the grow-up word goes around the others

parts.note: to grow up is to mature
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: Raising a child alone at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' is the adjective, as in a baby carrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby as an adjective means small-scale, so a miniature version.

clue.text: Female in Northern Ireland with time in AA

indicators.note: Northern Ireland with time go inside the two As

explanation.surface: A woman in Northern Ireland attending Alcoholics Anonymous for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a woman's given name, so a female.

clue.text: Old country house secured in 24 hours

indicators.note: held fast inside, so the house goes within the day

parts.note: 24 hours is a day
a house is a home

explanation.surface: A rural mansion locked up within a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was the former name of Benin in West Africa, so a country no longer existing.

clue.text: Complete report

definitions.meaning: as in 'safe and ...', whole and undamaged
a report is a noise, such as the bang of a gun

explanation.surface: A command to write up a full account.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means whole or intact, and also a noise heard, like a gun's report.

clue.text: Fresh crank's dismissed new London borough

parts.note: fresh, as of young or unripe things, means green

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the letter for new is removed from the crank

parts.note: a winch is turned by a crank handle; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A fresh eccentric is thrown out of some new London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crank' looks like an eccentric person but is a winding handle; WINCH minus N gives WICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is one of the boroughs of Greater London, home of the meridian.

clue.text: Briny solution in building material for complex construction

indicators.note: the shuffled briny letters sit inside the building material

parts.note: lath is thin strips of wood used in building walls

indicators.note: a solution is something dissolved and reformed, so the letters of briny are rearranged

explanation.surface: Salty water soaking into building material used in a complicated structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' suggests salt dissolved in brine, but here it signals the rearrangement of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is an intricate maze, the archetypal complex structure.

clue.text: Fear — that's Capone's weapon!

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster, so his first name is Al
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Dread at the sight of a gangster's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fright or anxiety at danger.

clue.text: Messages in echo Irishman sent back

parts.note: Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the Irishman's name is written backwards

parts.note: Liam is a common Irish man's name

explanation.surface: Messages bouncing back from an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Email as a mass noun means electronic messages collectively.

clue.text: Fish something worthless on its own?

parts.note: a lemon is a dud, something useless
sole means single, alone

explanation.surface: A dud fish left all by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a flatfish common in European waters.

clue.text: Reckoning track is needed on hike inland

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece being on another means it comes after it

parts.note: a hike is a rise, as in a price hike, so up
reckoning is counting, a count
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A route-counting walker plotting a trek into the interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is needed' only joins; in an across clue 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Upcountry means in or toward the interior of a country, away from the coast.

clue.text: Protestant man is appearing in court

indicators.note: a man appears in court, so the name and is go inside

parts.note: Alvin is a man's name

explanation.surface: A Protestant man appearing before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Calvinist follows John Calvin's Reformed theology, a branch of Protestantism.

clue.text: Stop unpleasant characters barring entrance in gallery

indicators.note: the trimmed pests go inside the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: excluding the first letter, the way in, of the pests

parts.note: vermin are obnoxious people

explanation.surface: Halting nasty types who are being kept out of a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barring entrance' reads as being refused entry, but it removes the first letter of the pests; the Tate is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to an end, to stop.

clue.text: Angry man I left after fuss about breadth of belly

indicators.note: the angry man and left come after the fuss in the answer
the fuss goes about, around, the letter for breadth

parts.note: fuss means ado

indicators.note: angry suggests agitated, so the letters of man I are stirred up

explanation.surface: A cross man complaining about the width of his stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal is the adjective meaning relating to the belly or stomach.

clue.text: Beer supporter drinks gallon in search for unknown

indicators.note: the beer takes in the gallon as if drinking it

parts.note: ale is beer
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A man downing a gallon of beer in pursuit of something mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra solves equations to find the value of an unknown quantity, x.

clue.text: Scarcity has many leaving planet

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for many is taken out

parts.note: a dearth is a scarcity
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A shortage driving crowds off the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is our home world, the third planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Report from German traders — leaders in Reichstag debate

parts.note: the Hansa or Hanseatic League was a medieval guild of German merchants

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters of these words

explanation.surface: A report of German merchants debating in the Reichstag.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansard is the official verbatim report of UK parliamentary debates.

clue.text: No particular interest shown around republic

indicators.note: turned around, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: one's bag is one's particular interest, as in 'not my bag'

explanation.surface: Nobody cares as a republic is given a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a West African nation governed as a republic.

clue.text: Lighter pole used by extremists in Guadeloupe

parts.note: a pole is a bar

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter pole used by Caribbean radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is the flat boat, not a fire-lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships.

clue.text: Without oxygen, maintain lively energy

indicators.note: lively suggests jumping about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Keeping up spirited energy despite lack of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like subtraction but here only joins O to the fodder: O and MAINTAIN are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness and vigour, a synonym of energy in its spirited sense.

clue.text: Hold-up man from great LA suburb

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A robber from a Los Angeles suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up man' suggests a robber; Atlas held up the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan Atlas was condemned to hold up the sky.

clue.text: Golden award framed by retro artist

indicators.note: the award sits inside the artist, like a picture in a frame

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A gold prize framed by an old-fashioned painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellow-gold colour, so golden in hue.

clue.text: Physicist's hesitant refusal to get into bunk with one

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: the hesitation and refusal go inside the bunk

parts.note: bunk is nonsense, as is bull
er is the sound of hesitation
no is a refusal
I is the Roman numeral one, added at the end

explanation.surface: A scientist hesitantly declining to share a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' means a bed in the surface but nonsense (BULL) in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Bernoulli was a Swiss physicist remembered for his principle of fluid flow.

clue.text: Pasty consumed by graduate master in Africa

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
pasty means pale, wan

explanation.surface: A pasty, the pie, eaten by a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' reads as the Cornish pie but is the adjective, WAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bwana is a Swahili form of address meaning sir or boss, used in East Africa.

clue.text: Eternal promise of face-cream factors?

definitions.meaning: anti-ageing creams promise their ingredients will make you look less old

explanation.surface: Advertising copy for a skin cream that claims to stop time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as AGE LESS, what a cream's factors promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless describes something that never grows old, hence eternal.

clue.text: Watered jungly plant

indicators.note: jungly suggests wild and tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something watered in a jungle-like garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarweed is a sticky-leaved American plant of the daisy family.
